## (2) Approaches message

Three things this design depends on are still missing or unchecked:
- **Owner field in report data.** The lookup is the report data model. No file was found, so it is not checkable.
- **Missing export action on the reports page.** The lookup is the page component. Its path is not in the gather draft, so it is not checkable from here.
- **10k-row timing baseline.** The lookup is a benchmark or a 10k-row fixture. Neither was found, so the under-60s row has no measured baseline.

**Owner-column row, again**

The ticket repair was cancelled at the shape-ticket gate, so the owner-column row comes back to you unchanged:

The ticket row "The export includes the owner column." conflicts with `src/export/csv.ts:40`, which has only title and status.
A) in-scope - add an owner column to the export
B) deviates: omit owner
C) deferred: acme/widgets#78
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77, because src/export/csv.ts:40 has no owner column
Recommendation: A - the row can ship in this gauntlet once an owner column is added. A change to the shared column list carries it to the export.

Until you answer, the row stays in-scope as written. The approaches below assume that.

**What separates the approaches**

The axis is where the owner column lives. It can go in the shared column list that the table and export both use, or only on the export.

**Recommendation: Approach 1, add owner to the shared column list.**

`csv.ts` already builds its columns from the table's definition. Adding `"owner"` to `tableColumns` keeps one column contract and lets the existing exporter carry it with no fork.

- The button sits beside the report title and calls the existing exporter.
- The cost is that the on-screen table also gains an owner column, which nobody asked for.
- It also depends on report records having an owner field, which is still unverified.
- The 10k-row row gets a timing test against a generated 10k-row report.

Removes: none
Adds: `"owner"` in `tableColumns` (`src/export/csv.ts:40`); Export CSV button beside the report title on the reports page component; click handler calling the existing CSV export; 10k-row timing test; owner-column export test
Pattern: follows the shared table/export column definition (`src/export/csv.ts:40`, per the gather draft).

**Approach 2 (reuse-only): add an export-only owner column to the existing exporter.**

The table stays as it is. `csv.ts` gains a parameter that adds owner after the table columns.

- This is a parameter on the existing construct, so it counts as reuse-only.
- Its blast radius is every other caller of `csv.ts`. I have not traced those callers, so that is unverified.
- It splits the single column contract into "table columns" plus "export extras". Later column changes then have two places to update.

Removes: none
Adds: an export-only extra-columns parameter in `src/export/csv.ts`; Export CSV button beside the report title; click handler passing `owner`; 10k-row timing test; owner-column export test
Pattern: cuts across the shared table/export column definition (`src/export/csv.ts:40`) by giving the export its own extra column.

**Option that changes the ask**

The candidate that drops the ask's assumption is Approach 1. It drops the unstated assumption that the visible table must not change.

**What would flip the recommendation**

- If the table must not show owner, I would switch to Approach 2.
- If your answer to the row question is B or C, the owner column drops out of both approaches. The work becomes pure wiring of the button to the existing exporter, with no column change.
